meta.title: THE LOCH NESS LOOP
meta.world: Loch Ness and the Great Glen
meta.style: Flat vector illustration, cel-shaded, solid flat colours and clean shapes, no outlines, soft long shadows; Highland light after rain, mid-September: loch-slate blue, heather and bracken orange, moss green, wet grey stone, one warm amber light in every frame; eye-level camera; 16:9

cover.title: THE LOCH NESS LOOP
cover.lead: Two days, a hired bike, the loop round Loch Ness. You make films in Zürich and last rode at film school. Shona has a yellow hybrid and a photo wall. Privately, you came for her.
cover.small: Single player · B2 · two forks, four endings

hotspot.object: the yellow hybrid bike on the shingle at Dores

briefing.title: THE WORDS FOR A BIKE

cards.head: THE WHEEL
cards.text: TYRE · INNER TUBE · VALVE · RIM · SPOKES · HUB

cards.head: THE DRIVE
cards.text: CHAIN · CHAINRING · CASSETTE · DERAILLEUR · CRANK · PEDALS

cards.head: THE CONTROLS
cards.text: HANDLEBARS · BRAKE LEVERS · BRAKE PADS · GEAR SHIFTERS

cards.head: THE FRAME AND THE REST
cards.text: TOP TUBE · SEAT POST · SADDLE · MUDGUARD · PANNIER RACK

cards.head: THE VERBS
cards.text: PUMP UP · CHANGE DOWN · COME OFF · RUB · SLIP

briefing.note: On a British bike the RIGHT lever is the FRONT brake, the opposite of most of the world. Both levers, gently, every time.

hotspot.object: the yellow hybrid at the counter

shop1.title: THE TERMS
shop1.story: Shona wheels it to the counter. "Two days, forty pounds. Back by six tomorrow or it's a third day, and that's twenty more. Hundred deposit, cash."
shop1.clue: Your train home leaves at eight tomorrow evening; you were planning to ride in at seven.
shop1.prompt: What does riding in at seven cost you?
shop1.explanation: Shona said "back by six tomorrow or it's a third day", and a third day is "twenty more". Seven is after six.

hotspot.object: the e-bike's battery

shop2.title: WHICH BIKE
shop2.story: "Forty miles on a charge, and the loop is sixty-six. I'd not take the e-bike if I were you. The yellow one's lighter and it doesn't run out."
shop2.clue: Shona taps the e-bike's battery: the charge light is green, fully charged, right now.
shop2.prompt: Which bike is she telling you to take, and why?

answers.text: The e-bike: the charge light is on green
The yellow: the e-bike won't do the loop
The yellow: it will do forty miles a day

shop2.explanation: "I'd not take the e-bike if I were you" is advice against it: "forty miles on a charge" is short of the loop's sixty-six.

hotspot.object: the saddle on the workstand

shop3.title: KNEE JUST BENT
shop3.story: She stands you astride it, phone ready for the wall. "Knee just bent at the bottom. Flick the lever under the saddle and slide it up an inch."
shop3.clue: The saddle sits on a tube that slides into the frame; a small lever clamps it.
shop3.prompt: What does Shona want you to slide up?
shop3.explanation: The SEAT POST carries the saddle and slides down into the SEAT TUBE, the frame tube that holds it. A "rod" is a translation.

hotspot.object: the right-hand brake lever

shop4.title: THE RIGHT LEVER
shop4.story: Her hands over yours. "Right one's the front brake here, not like at home. Grab that alone on a hill and you're over the handlebars. Squeeze both."
shop4.clue: Two blades under your fingers, one each side of the handlebars; you squeeze them towards you.
shop4.prompt: What is she telling you to squeeze, both at once?
shop4.explanation: BRAKE LEVERS: a lever pivots when you squeeze it. "Handles" and "grips" are translations; the GRIPS are the rubber ends of the handlebars.

hotspot.object: the rear derailleur

shop5.title: THE WEE ARM
shop5.story: Shona clicks the shifter and turns the pedal. "Watch the back wheel. That wee arm's what moves the chain across the cogs. Bend it and you're walking."
shop5.clue: A sprung arm under the cogs on the back wheel, with two tiny wheels inside it.
shop5.prompt: What is the arm that moves the chain called?
shop5.explanation: The DERAILLEUR is the arm that pushes the chain sideways. The CASSETTE is the stack of cogs it crosses; the CHAINRINGS sit at the pedals.

hotspot.object: the loaded bike at the railing over the river

shop6.title: LORRIES AND NO VERGE
shop6.story: Outside, she points down the river. "Out through Dores, loch on your right, and keep it there all the way round. Not the A82. Lorries, and no verge."
shop6.clue: Two roads leave town: over the bridge to Dores, or straight down onto the A82.
shop6.prompt: Which road, and which side is the water on?

answers.text: Through Dores, with water on your left
Down the A82, with water on your right
Over the bridge, water on your right

shop6.explanation: "Out through Dores" is the road over the bridge, and the loch stays "on your right". "Not the A82" rules the other road out.

hotspot.object: the flat back tyre

shore1.title: FLAT BY THE WATER
shore1.story: Two miles past Dores the back of the bike goes soft and wanders. You stop by the water. A thorn stands out of the rubber like a nail.
shore1.clue: The outer rubber that meets the road, not the soft tube inside; the thorn is there.
shore1.prompt: You ring the shop. "Shona, there's a thorn in ___."
shore1.explanation: The thorn is in the TYRE, the outer rubber. The INNER TUBE is the soft ring that holds the air, and the RIM is metal.

hotspot.object: the front wheel at the cattle grid

hill1.title: THE CATTLE GRID
hill1.story: The high road: sheep, a cattle grid you hit too fast, and then a wobble in the front wheel, side to side, that was not there before.
hill1.clue: One thin wire between the hub and the rim is slack; it twangs like a string.
hill1.prompt: What has the cattle grid loosened?
hill1.explanation: A SPOKE is a wire under tension; one slack and the RIM wobbles. The HUB is the centre, and "radius" is a translation.

hotspot.object: the tyre lever hooked under the tyre

shore2.title: TWO PLASTIC HOOKS
shore2.story: In the saddlebag: a spare tube, a mini pump, and two flat plastic hooks. You have never used them. You know exactly what they are for.
shore2.clue: Slide one under the tyre's edge, hook it on a spoke, work the other along.
shore2.prompt: What are the two plastic hooks called?
shore2.explanation: TYRE LEVERS lever the tyre over the rim; "lifters" is a translation. A SPOKE KEY is a tiny spanner that tightens spokes.

hotspot.object: the mini pump on the valve

hill2.title: SIXTY ON THE BACK
hill2.story: Whitebridge. The tyres squash like porridge. You text Shona a photo of the mini pump on the valve. Back in seconds: "Sixty on the back. All of it."
hill2.clue: A hundred strokes on the pump gets you there; the tyre goes hard under your thumb.
hill2.prompt: What is she telling you to do to the back tyre?
hill2.explanation: PUMP UP is the verb and the number follows TO. "Until" wants an event, not a figure; "at sixty" is a translation.

hotspot.object: the club rider's orange jersey

shore3.title: THE ORANGE JERSEY
shore3.story: A rider in an orange jersey slows beside you, thumbs your back tyre. "Forty? You'll pinch that on the first pothole past Foyers. Sixty-five, at least. Cheerio."
shore3.clue: The pump got heavy at forty, so you stopped. A pinch: the rim cuts the tube.
shore3.prompt: What is he warning will happen at forty?

answers.text: The tyre bursting on the descent
A second puncture, cut by the rim

shore3.explanation: "You'll pinch that on the first pothole": the rim cuts the tube when the tyre is soft. Another flat, not a burst.

hotspot.object: the farmer's red quad bike at the gate

hill3.title: THE FARMER'S GATE
hill3.story: A farmer on a quad bike holds the gate. "Four miles down to Fort Augustus and it's all brakes. The café at the top's your last. Mind yourself."
hill3.clue: The red quad bike idles at the gate. Your bottle is empty; the road drops away.
hill3.prompt: What is the farmer telling you, in plain words?

answers.text: Buy what you need now; nothing below
There's a second café four miles down
Push the bike down the steepest parts

hill3.explanation: "The café at the top's your last" means no more café below, and "all brakes" says the road drops. Get what you need here.

hotspot.object: the chain hanging off the chainring

shore4.title: THE CLIMB OUT OF FOYERS
shore4.story: The climb out of Foyers is a wall. You stand on the pedals, click for an easier gear, and your feet spin on nothing. The chain hangs loose.
shore4.clue: The chain dangles below the big ring at the pedals; its teeth are bare.
shore4.prompt: You ring the shop. What has happened?
shore4.explanation: The verb is COMES OFF: the chain leaves the CHAINRING and hangs. "Fallen" and "gone out" are translated, and nobody on a bike says them.

hotspot.object: the cassette on the back wheel

hill4.title: THE LONG DRAG
hill4.story: The drag after Whitebridge. You push on the pedals and the back end lurches: the chain lets go of its cog under your weight, catches, lets go again.
hill4.clue: It only happens under load; soft pedalling on the flat, the stack of cogs is fine.
hill4.prompt: You text Shona. The gears keep doing what?
hill4.explanation: Gears SLIP: the chain loses its grip on the cog under load. "Sliding" and "escaping" are translations, and a worn CASSETTE is the usual cause.

hotspot.object: Moira's pint glass under the bar lamp

pub1.title: DUTCH, THEN DANISH
pub1.story: Moira, into her pint: "Dutch. No - Danish. You've the look." You: "Swiss." Jean, from the other stool: "Whereabouts? The German bit or the French bit?"
pub1.clue: Moira's pint glass sits under the lamp; Jean has not looked up from her half.
pub1.prompt: What is Jean asking you for?

answers.text: Which part of Switzerland you come from
A straight yes or no to Moira's guesses
How many languages you grew up speaking

pub1.explanation: "Whereabouts" asks for the place inside the country; "the German bit or the French bit" are regions of Switzerland, not languages.

hotspot.object: the pub window with the loch at dusk

pub2.title: FLAT AS A PLATE
pub2.story: Moira: "The bay at first light, flat calm. Twice I've seen her." Jean: "Off the castle, the back of six, if you must. Calm, or nothing."
pub2.clue: The loch out the window lies flat as a plate. Back of six: just past six.
pub2.prompt: What do the two women actually agree on?

answers.text: Any time, as long as it's calm
Dawn, and only on a calm loch
Six o'clock, and off the castle

pub2.explanation: Moira says "first light" and "flat calm"; Jean says "back of six" and "calm, or nothing". Same time, same water; only the place differs.

hotspot.object: the rear brake on the bike by the pub door

pub3.title: JEAN AND THE MULTI-TOOL
pub3.story: Jean heard it from the bar. Outside she spins the back wheel: a whisper every turn. "Rubbing. Two minutes." A multi-tool from her coat. "Archie. The pier, six."
pub3.clue: Two rubber blocks either side of the rim, and one is touching. Archie has a boat.
pub3.prompt: What does Jean say is rubbing?
pub3.explanation: BRAKE PADS are the rubber blocks that grip the rim; one out of line rubs. LEVERS are at your hands, CABLES only pull.

hotspot.object: Archie's hand on the tiller

deep1.title: RULES ABOARD
deep1.story: Archie's hand on the tiller. "Rules. Sit low. Nobody stands, nobody shouts. Camera stays below the rail till I say. She hears a boat before she sees it."
deep1.clue: The rail is the boat's wooden edge; his hand on the tiller has not moved.
deep1.prompt: When does the camera come above the rail?
deep1.explanation: "Camera stays below the rail till I say": the signal is his word, not her appearing. Sitting low is a separate rule.

hotspot.object: the gulls on the flat water

bay1.title: ENGINE OFF
bay1.story: Archie cuts the engine and the bay goes silent. "Nobody talks now. If the birds lift, you look where they came from, not where they're going."
bay1.clue: Thirty gulls sit on the water off the reeds; the launch drifts, and nobody has spoken.
bay1.prompt: The gulls all lift at once. Where do you look?

answers.text: At the water they have just left
Ahead of them, where they fly to
Up at the thirty birds themselves

bay1.explanation: "Look where they came from, not where they're going": the birds flee something, so the something is under the spot they left.

hotspot.object: the orange strap over the pannier rack

deep2.title: THE ORANGE STRAP
deep2.story: The bike lies in the bow. Archie throws you a strap. "Round the frame over the back wheel, where your bags hang. Not the thin bit. It'll tear."
deep2.clue: An orange strap over the metal frame above the back wheel, where the bags clip on.
deep2.prompt: What is Archie telling you to strap it by?
deep2.explanation: The PANNIER RACK holds the bags and takes a strap. A MUDGUARD is thin and tears; a CHAIN GUARD sits at the pedals.

hotspot.object: the front wheel off, leaning on the thwart

bay2.title: TEN SECONDS
bay2.story: The bike won't fit past the thwart with the front wheel on. Archie nods at the small lever at the hub. "Flip that. Wheel's off in ten seconds."
bay2.clue: The front wheel leans on the thwart, the bench across the boat, its lever flipped open.
bay2.prompt: What did you do to get the wheel off?
bay2.explanation: The QUICK RELEASE is the cam lever that clamps the wheel into the FORK, and you UNDO it. "Quick lock" and "fast lever" are translations.

hotspot.object: the wet back and white wake, castle behind

deep3.title: NOT THIS ONE
deep3.story: Fifty yards off, a wet back and a wake. Archie, barely audible: "She'll go down. She'll come up once more, further off. That's your picture. Not this one."
deep3.clue: The castle on its rock behind her; the white wake is already moving away from you.
deep3.prompt: When does Archie want you to take the photo?

answers.text: Once she is fifty yards off

deep3.explanation: "She'll come up once more, further off. That's your picture. Not this one": wait for the next surfacing, even though it is further away.

hotspot.object: the neck against the sunrise

bay3.title: COUNT TO TWENTY
bay3.story: A wake crosses the bay, nothing in front of it. A neck lifts against the sunrise. Archie, under his breath: "Count. Over twenty seconds up, that's no seal."
bay3.clue: You count under your breath. At nineteen the neck is still up; at twenty-four it goes.
bay3.prompt: What does your count tell you it was?

answers.text: A seal, but a very big one
Not a seal, whatever it is

bay3.explanation: "Over twenty seconds up, that's no seal": it went at twenty-four, so by Archie's rule it is something else. What, he does not say.

hotspot.object: the bent rear mudguard

back1.title: TICK, TICK
back1.story: Archie puts you off below the castle. On the walkers' path, something ticks once a turn at the back wheel, like a card in the spokes.
back1.clue: The curved strip over the back wheel that keeps spray off your back has bent inwards.
back1.prompt: What has bent in? You'll need the word for Shona.
back1.explanation: A MUDGUARD stops the wheel throwing water up your back; bent in, it touches the tyre. A REFLECTOR is flat and only shines back light.

hotspot.object: the notes on the shop counter

back2.title: THE COUNT
back2.story: Shona runs a thumb down the sheet. "Scratch on the top tube - that was on already. Mudguard's new, fifteen. Kit's all there." She counts notes out.
back2.clue: A hundred went down in cash on Wednesday. It is ten past twelve on Thursday.
back2.prompt: How much comes back across the counter?
back2.explanation: "That was on already" means the scratch is not yours; "new, fifteen" is the only charge. A hundred less fifteen is eighty-five.

hotspot.object: the fork in the road above the beach

dores.title: THE FORK AT DORES
dores.story: Dores beach, late morning, the water flat and grey. Above the shingle the road splits: along the shore, or up over the moor. Both end at Fort Augustus.

choices.label: ALONG THE WATER
choices.note: By the water, a waterfall, a café, one steep climb out of Foyers.

choices.label: UP OVER THE MOOR
choices.note: Sheep, cattle grids, one farm and no shop; a long descent at the end.

hotspot.object: the lamp on Archie's launch

pier.title: SIX AT THE PIER
pier.story: Six, and the loch is a mirror. Archie MacRae waits in a wooden launch, lamp lit. "The castle, deep water. Or the bay, shallow. You pay the diesel."

choices.label: OUT TO THE CASTLE
choices.note: An hour up the loch; deep water, the sonar ground, and rules aboard.

choices.label: DRIFT INTO THE BAY
choices.note: Ten minutes out, engine off, weed and birds; you keep your mouth shut.

master.label: ON THE WALL
master.title: THAT'S HER
master.text: Shona zooms in on the third photo and says nothing for a long time. "That's her." She pins it on the wall, next to the one of you astride the yellow bike, and hands over eighty-five pounds. Train at eight.

hotspot.object: the photo pinned on the shop wall

complete.label: LOOP COMPLETE
complete.title: AYE, THAT'S THE LOCH
complete.text: The third photo is a wake and rain on the lens. Shona looks at it properly, which is something. "Aye, that's the loch." Eighty-five pounds back, legs that will hurt tomorrow, and a train at eight.

hotspot.object: the phone on the counter

missing.label: PHOTOS MISSING
missing.title: THE PICTURE NOT TAKEN
missing.text: The loop is done and the phone was in the bag when it mattered. Shona hands the deposit back and asks what you saw. You tell her: the back, the wake, the neck. She has heard it before. She nods anyway.

hotspot.object: the phone in the open pannier on the counter

failed.label: OUT OF CHANCES
failed.title: HOME ON THE BUS
failed.text: The bike comes home on the rack of the bus from Fort Augustus, you in the seat behind it. Shona counts the kit and does not ask. Out of the window the loch keeps herself to herself.

hotspot.object: the bike on the rack of the bus
